name: io.github.2016judea/tip-overtime-w2
title: Tip & Overtime Deductions
description: Works out the no-tax-on-tips and no-tax-on-overtime deductions and W-2 boxes, with the math shown

tools.name: tip_overtime_deduction
tools.description: Works out the federal 'no tax on tips' and 'no tax on overtime' deductions (Schedule 1-A, Form 1040, tax years 2025-2028) from what the person has: W-2 box 12 code TP and TT and box 14b, Form 4137, 1099s, or pay stubs before the W-2 arrives (hours over 40 and hourly rate, or overtime pay and its multiplier). Returns each deduction with the math line by line as it goes on Schedule 1-A, the Form 1040 line it lands on, the estimated federal income tax saved, what is still unknown, a citation for every rule, and a worksheet link that opens the filled-in Schedule 1-A worksheet to print or hand to a preparer. Use for 'how much of my tips can I deduct', 'does no tax on overtime apply to me', 'what goes on Schedule 1-A', 'I made $X in tips as a server'. Only the FLSA half of time-and-a-half counts as qualified overtime. Married filing separately gets nothing. Pass dollar amounts as numbers. Filing status and income (AGI) set the phase-out and the tax-saved estimate; without them the result says what is missing instead of assuming them.

filing_status.description: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately), hoh (head of household), qss (qualifying surviving spouse)

agi.description: Adjusted gross income (Form 1040 line 11b), dollars. Used as MAGI unless magi is given.

magi.description: Modified AGI if different: AGI plus excluded Puerto Rico / foreign earned income (Schedule 1-A line 3)

valid_ssn.description: false if the person (or the spouse who earned the tips/overtime) has no Social Security number valid for work. Default true.

employer.description: A label for the job, e.g. 'restaurant'. Not stored.

box12_tp.description: W-2 box 12 code TP: cash tips reported to the employer

box14b.description: W-2 box 14b Treasury Tipped Occupation Code(s), e.g. '102' or '101 000'

nonqualified_tips.description: Part of TP earned in an occupation NOT on the IRS list (only when 14b shows 000)

form4137_tips.description: Form 4137 line 1 column (c) for this employer: all cash and charge tips received, if Form 4137 is filed

tips_paystub.description: Tips from pay stubs, year to date, when there is no W-2 yet (estimate)

box12_tt.description: W-2 box 12 code TT: qualified overtime

ot_hours_over_40.description: Without a W-2: total hours over 40 in a workweek across the year

regular_rate.description: Without a W-2: regular hourly rate, dollars

ot_pay_total.description: Without a W-2: total overtime pay shown on stubs (the whole 1.5x or 2x amount)

ot_premium_paid.description: Without a W-2: only the premium part above regular pay, if the stub shows it separately

ot_multiplier.description: Overtime pay multiple: 1.5 (default) or 2 for double time

flsa_exempt.description: true if exempt from FLSA overtime (e.g. salaried manager): nothing qualifies

self_employed.description: Tips earned in the person's own business (1099s).

other_deductions.description: Other deductions allocable to that business

ot_1099.description: Qualified overtime on Form 1099-NEC box 1d / 1099-MISC box 14

tools.name: w2_tip_overtime_boxes
tools.description: For an owner, bookkeeper or payroll person: works out the new 2026 Form W-2 figures for each employee from payroll rows: box 12 code TP (cash tips reported to the employer), box 12 code TT (qualified overtime: hours over 40 in each FLSA workweek x 0.5 x the regular rate, where the regular rate includes non-discretionary bonuses, tip credit and service charges paid out) and box 14b (Treasury Tipped Occupation Code, suggested from the role). Pass one row per employee per workweek, as rows or as a pasted CSV/tab table with a header (employee, week_start, hours, rate, tips, role; optional tip_credit, other_pay, service_charges, ttoc, exempt). Returns per-employee boxes, every overtime week with its math, flags, and a link to a printable sheet. W-2s for 2026 are due January 31, 2027.

table.description: Pasted CSV or tab-separated table with a header row

employee.description: Name or initials (initials are fine; nothing is stored)

week_start.description: First day of the FLSA workweek, YYYY-MM-DD. All rows must start on the same weekday.

tools.name: tipped_occupation_code
tools.description: Finds the Treasury Tipped Occupation Code (W-2 box 14b) for a job title, from the IRS list of 71 occupations that customarily received tips before 2025, with the IRS description and examples, the related SOC code, and what the tips deduction is worth at that occupation's median pay (BLS OEWS May 2025): federal income tax saved per $1,000 of tips and the most it can save in a year. Use for 'does my job qualify for no tax on tips', 'what is my tipped occupation code', 'is a barista a tipped occupation'. Pass a job title, or a 3-digit code.

job.description: Job title in the user's words, or a 3-digit TTOC

tools.name: no_tax_on_tips_savings
tools.description:
What the federal 'no tax on tips' deduction is worth for a year of tips: the deduction (up to $25,000), the estimated federal income tax it saves, the Schedule 1-A lines, and whether the job is on the IRS list of tipped occupations. Takes the year's tips and, optionally, the job, filing status and income. Same engine as tip_overtime_deduction, for someone who has a tips figure but no W-2 yet.

Example questions:
- "I'm a server and made $18,000 in tips, how much will no tax on tips save me?"
- "How much is no tax on tips worth for a bartender making $45k?"
- "Will the tips deduction get me a bigger refund?"

tips.description: Cash and card tips for the year, dollars (W-2 box 12 TP if they have it)

job.description: Job title in the user's words, e.g. 'server', 'hair stylist'

filing_status.description: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately), hoh (head of household), qss (qualifying surviving spouse)

agi.description: Adjusted gross income (Form 1040 line 11b), dollars. If unknown, total yearly pay is a fair stand-in.

tools.name: no_tax_on_overtime_savings
tools.description:
What the federal 'no tax on overtime' deduction is worth: only the half in time-and-a-half counts, capped at $12,500 ($25,000 joint). Takes overtime hours and hourly rate, or the overtime pay on the stubs, or W-2 box 12 TT; returns the deduction, the estimated federal income tax saved, the Schedule 1-A lines and a worksheet link. Same engine as tip_overtime_deduction.

Example questions:
- "I worked 300 hours of overtime at $24 an hour, how much is no tax on overtime worth?"
- "My stubs show $9,000 of overtime pay, what can I deduct?"
- "Does double time count for no tax on overtime?"

overtime_hours.description: Hours over 40 in a workweek, added up for the year

overtime_pay.description: Total overtime pay on the stubs for the year (the whole 1.5x or 2x amount)

box12_tt.description: W-2 box 12 code TT, if they have the W-2

salaried_exempt.description: true if FLSA-exempt (most salaried managers): nothing qualifies

filing_status.description: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately), hoh (head of household), qss (qualifying surviving spouse)

agi.description: Adjusted gross income (Form 1040 line 11b), dollars. If unknown, total yearly pay is a fair stand-in.

tools.name: no_tax_on_tips_income_limit
tools.description:
The income phase-out for both deductions at one income: the threshold ($150,000, or $300,000 joint), how much each deduction is cut ($100 per $1,000 over), the most each can still be, and the income at which each reaches zero. Optional tips and overtime figures make it exact for the person; without them it uses the caps ($25,000 tips, $12,500 / $25,000 overtime). Married filing separately gets neither.

Example questions:
- "Is there an income limit for no tax on tips?"
- "I make $210,000, do I still get no tax on overtime?"
- "At what income does the tips deduction phase out for married couples?"

filing_status.description: single, mfj (married filing jointly), mfs (married filing separately), hoh (head of household), qss (qualifying surviving spouse)

tips.description: Qualified tips for the year, if known

overtime.description: Qualified overtime (the half portion), if known

tools.name: which_tips_qualify
tools.description:
The rules for what counts as a qualified tip, each with the statute or regulation's own words and a link: the job has to be on the IRS list of tipped occupations, service charges and automatic gratuities are not tips, the $25,000 cap per return, the income phase-out, the joint-return and Social Security number requirements, the limit for self-employed tips, and the 2025-2028 window. With a job title it also checks the IRS list.

Example questions:
- "Do automatic gratuities count as tips for the deduction?"
- "Is no tax on tips permanent?"
- "Do I still pay Social Security on my tips?"
- "Do my tips as a barista qualify?"

job.description: Optional job title to check against the IRS list

tools.name: which_overtime_qualifies
tools.description:
The rules for qualified overtime, each with the statute, IRS notice or W-2 instruction's own words and a link: only overtime the federal Fair Labor Standards Act requires (over 40 hours in a workweek), only the half in time-and-a-half, nothing for FLSA-exempt (most salaried) employees, the $12,500 / $25,000 joint cap, joint returns only, and the income phase-out.

Example questions:
- "Does no tax on overtime cover the whole time and a half?"
- "I'm salaried, do I get no tax on overtime?"
- "Does California daily overtime count?"

tools.name: self_employed_tips_deduction
tools.description:
The 'no tax on tips' deduction for tips earned in the person's own business, reported on a 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC or 1099-K: counted only up to the business's profit, with the Schedule 1-A lines, the estimated federal income tax saved and a worksheet link. Same engine as tip_overtime_deduction.

Example questions:
- "I drive for Uber, do my tips count for no tax on tips?"
- "I rent a salon chair and get tips on a 1099, can I deduct them?"
- "DoorDash tips and no tax on tips"

tools.name: schedule_1a_how_to_fill

Schedule 1-A (Form 1040) Parts II and III filled in line by line from the person's W-2 or pay figures, with the Form 1040 line the total lands on and a worksheet link that opens the filled-in schedule to print. Takes the same fields as tip_overtime_deduction; leads with the lines.

Example questions:
- "How do I fill out Schedule 1-A?"
- "What goes on Schedule 1-A line 4?"

tools.name: w2_box_12_tp_tt_explained
tools.description:
What the new W-2 entries mean for the tips and overtime deductions, with the IRS instructions' own words: box 12 code TP (cash tips reported to the employer), box 12 code TT (qualified overtime, the half portion only), box 14b (the Treasury Tipped Occupation Code, 000 for a job not on the list), and the due date for 2026 W-2s. With a role it suggests the box 14b code.

Example questions:
- "What is code TT on my W-2?"
- "My W-2 box 14b says 000, what does that mean?"
- "When do employers have to send W-2s with the new boxes?"

role.description: Optional job title, to suggest its box 14b code
